rationale: One localized defect in new-inode ownership. mkdir02 asserts the POSIX rule Linux implements in inode_init_owner: a directory created inside a parent with S_ISGID set inherits the parent's GID, and (being a directory) also inherits the S_ISGID bit. Asterinas implements neither half. Both filesystems set the new inode's GID unconditionally from the creator's credentials with no reference to the parent: ramfs via current_fs_ids() -> credentials.fsgid() (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ramfs/fs.rs:1453-1461) and ext2 via credentials.fsgid() in its create path (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ext2/fs.rs:394-409). Nothing in kernel/src/fs/ reads a parent's S_ISGID for inheritance; the only has_set_gid() callers are the hardlink CAP_FOWNER check (vfs/path/mod.rs:306) and a mount flag. So both of the test's two assertions fail from the same missing rule, and the fix is one parent-directory check at inode creation rather than two unrelated changes. Narrow, well-specified semantics over a subsystem Asterinas lacks. Chosen over the alternatives I ruled out below.
notes: Evidence: host=pass measured this round on the pinned LTP 20260529 prebuilt (TPASS 'New dir inherited GID and S_ISGID'), run from a temp dir copied out of the Nix store. Asterinas probe=fail at this run's exact base_commit e8f2b9ca6, recorded independently by run-rVlQYu and run-IsX1sM, so it is usable as-is and not re-probed; no Asterinas boot was spent this round. Uncovered ground: rounds 1-9 took fsync03, llseek01, socket01, setpriority02, dup02, timerfd_gettime01, clock_getres01, brk02, renameat202, epoll_ctl02 and gvisor readv_test, none touching ownership/permission inheritance. Ruled out from the same 74-candidate probe-fail set at e8f2b9ca6: mincore01-04, splice01/02 and tee01 (mincore/splice/tee absent from the syscall table in kernel/src/syscall/arch/x86.rs, so missing-feature verdicts); pipe2_04 (needs F_SETPIPE_SZ/F_GETPIPE_SZ 1031/1032, absent from FcntlCmd in kernel/src/syscall/fcntl.rs); fcntl23/fcntl27 (F_SETLEASE, a whole lease subsystem); utimes01 (needs_rofs, read-only mount infrastructure); mprotect01 (its ENOMEM and EACCES cases look like two separate defects, not one); getcpu01 (would turn on scheduler migration semantics, broader than one check). mkdir02 is an all.txt entry, so it runs at the default CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/tmp (ramfs) and run_vars is empty; the ramfs path is what verify will exercise, though the same rule is missing in ext2 and a fix covering both would be the honest one. 67 other LTP stale-entry passes sit in the cache as cheap pool-only edits, not taken here because a real defect is the better use of the final round. Suite priority put ltp first and its pool is far from empty (976 commented in all.txt, 70 in blocked/exfat.txt, 2 in blocked/ext2.txt); kselftest excluded by the user for this round. The discarded select.json.kselftest-discarded in this run directory was not read.
